won.source: PTC News, 2 December 2003 (promotions/ptc/archive/news-2003-12.html): "Can Saij continue his run of form that led to him winning the Chris Williams Memorial Cup?" — the tournament's own conclusion, recapped from a fourth promotion's vantage.

conflict.reading_a: PTC's own contemporary news of 2 December 2003 reports Saij winning the Cup that year — the only dated winner the surviving record confirms.
conflict.reading_b: Jay Phoenix's own PCW biography card (promotions/pcw/archive/jay-phoenix-bio.html) and PRIME biography card instead claim a Chris Williams Memorial Cup championship of his own, the PCW card dating it "2003" under a PWW heading. PRIME's ReVolution 197 (17 June 2009, an in-fiction interview question) and SCCW's own match-segment 20053 (8 March 2009, his entrance video) separately bill him a two-time Cup winner. None of the three claims names a specific staging, an opponent, or a result any other federation's record corroborates.

title: cwmc-chris-williams-memorial-cup
label: The Illustrious Face-Eater

won.source: The PTC forum's own Chris Williams Memorial Cup Official Forum, "CWMC 2007 Results" (post 245831, 12 September 2007): "your 2007 Chris William's Memorial Cup Winner: THE ILLUSTRIOUS FACE-EATER," three judges to none over Digital Mortality. A second, independent receipt on a different surface, five months later: fwrestling.com's own community wrestler voting list (posted 6 January 2008, /promotions/fwrestling/archive/fwrestling-com-wrestler-voting-list-2008-01-06.html), whose entry for The Illustrious Face-Eater reads, entire: "2007 Accomplishments: Won Chris Williams Memorial Cup — Leagues: TEAM."

how: Six rounds and a Second Chance Battle Royal wildcard across 34 entrants, run in Flagstaff, Arizona as "the first ever PTC Indy Event," organised in-fiction by Jay Phoenix.
